comments.author: martin-lindstrom
comments.body: If we update RFC7733 with support for OIDC, we only have one specification for certificate authentication contexts ...

comments.author: martin-lindstrom
comments.body:
Under "About the document":
> _The latest revision of this draft can be found at https://swedenconnect.github.io/ietf-rfc7773-oidc-auth-context/draft-santesson-oidc-certificate-authentication-context.html._ 

Perhaps use "official" Sweden Connect hostname? https://docs.swedenconnect.se/ietf-rfc7773-oidc-auth-context/draft-santesson-oidc-certificate-authentication-context.html?

comments.author: martin-lindstrom
comments.body:
From "Introduction":
> _The extension is a sequence of AuthenticationContext structures, each identified by a contextType URI that also determines the syntax of the accompanying contextInfo string. [[RFC7773](https://docs.swedenconnect.se/ietf-rfc7773-oidc-auth-context/draft-santesson-oidc-certificate-authentication-context.html#RFC7773)] defines one context type, SAML Authentication Context Information (SACI), for subjects authenticated by a SAML assertion, and explicitly provides for other documents to define additional context types.[¶](https://docs.swedenconnect.se/ietf-rfc7773-oidc-auth-context/draft-santesson-oidc-certificate-authentication-context.html#section-1-2)_

Given this, one could say that our current document declares a new context type... So, name it "Certificate Authentication Context Type for OpenID Connect" instead? By doing so, it is more clear that this document extends RFC7773.

comments.author: martin-lindstrom
comments.body:
From Introduction:
> _OpenID Connect [[OIDC.Core](https://docs.swedenconnect.se/ietf-rfc7773-oidc-auth-context/draft-santesson-oidc-certificate-authentication-context.html#OIDC.Core)] has become a widely deployed alternative to SAML for federated authentication. An OpenID Connect authentication results in an ID Token, a JSON Web Token [[RFC7519](https://docs.swedenconnect.se/ietf-rfc7773-oidc-auth-context/draft-santesson-oidc-certificate-authentication-context.html#RFC7519)] containing claims about the authentication event and the authenticated End-User._

Yes, this is true, BUT. The ID Token normally contains the `sub` claim, and other identity claims are delivered after a call to the UserInfo endpoint. Maybe mention this?

comments.author: martin-lindstrom
comments.body:
From "Introduction":
> _a context type whose contextInfo is a JSON object [[RFC8259](https://docs.swedenconnect.se/ietf-rfc7773-oidc-auth-context/draft-santesson-oidc-certificate-authentication-context.html#RFC8259)] carrying the information from an ID Token that is relevant to the issuance of a certificate.[](https://docs.swedenconnect.se/ietf-rfc7773-oidc-auth-context/draft-santesson-oidc-certificate-authentication-context.html#section-1-3)_

... carrying the information from an ID Token and possibly a UserInfo response that are relevant ...

comments.author: martin-lindstrom
comments.body:
From "Introduction":
> _and a mapping from ID Token claims to the subject name attributes of the certificate that were derived from them.[](https://docs.swedenconnect.se/ietf-rfc7773-oidc-auth-context/draft-santesson-oidc-certificate-authentication-context.html#section-1-4)_

... and a mapping from ID Token and UserInfo claims to the subject name ....

comments.author: martin-lindstrom
comments.body:
Section 3.3, "JSON Structure":
> _`auth_time`: String. The time at which the End-User authentication occurred, taken from the auth_time claim of the ID Token. The value is expressed as a date-time string according to [[RFC3339](https://docs.swedenconnect.se/ietf-rfc7773-oidc-auth-context/draft-santesson-oidc-certificate-authentication-context.html#RFC3339)] in UTC, using the "Z" time zone designator and without fractional seconds, e.g. 2026-10-19T13:04:05Z. If the ID Token contains no auth_time claim, this member is absent. This member corresponds to the AuthenticationInstant attribute of SACI.[¶](https://docs.swedenconnect.se/ietf-rfc7773-oidc-auth-context/draft-santesson-oidc-certificate-authentication-context.html#section-3.3-2.4.1)_

In OIDC the `auth_time` is an integer (seconds since epoch). Why change this to something else?

Also, the `auth_time` is not always present in the ID Token (it depends whether the RP actually requested it), so that should also be highlighted.

comments.author: martin-lindstrom
comments.body:
Section 3.3, "JSON Structure":
> _`acr`: Array of strings. The Authentication Context Class Reference values satisfied by the authentication. The array MUST contain at least one element when present. In most cases the array contains exactly one element, the value of the acr claim of the ID Token. A CA MAY list more than one value when it has determined that the performed authentication satisfies more than one authentication context class; how such a determination is made is out of scope for this document. The array carries no ordering semantics. This member corresponds to the AuthnContextClassRef attribute of SACI.[](https://docs.swedenconnect.se/ietf-rfc7773-oidc-auth-context/draft-santesson-oidc-certificate-authentication-context.html#section-3.3-2.6.1)_

I don't understand why we would like to have an array. An authentication always maps to exactly **one** ACR-value.

comments.author: martin-lindstrom
comments.body:

I am missing the `sub` claim. Either we mention that `sub` MUST be included in `claim_mappings`, or (my suggestion), include it at the top level.
